1527009.title: LAN: Bypass Guest Authentication
1527009.expected results:
The website should be accessible from the LAN without getting redirected to the Authentication page when this option is enabled:

1. Both LAN client a and b can PING the WAN host IP. 
2. Only LAN client b can access the WAN host IP.
3. Listbox beside Bypass Guest Authentication get dimmed.
4. Both client cannot ping the WAN host IP. You need to authenticate yourself first before accessing internet.
1527009.initial setup:
WAN host-------TZ180W---------LAN client a 
| 
| 
| 
LAN client b
1527009.steps:
1. Go to Network->Zones->LAN Zone, edit LAN zone, enable Guest Service and Bypass Guest Authentication: All MAC Addresses. 
2. Verify if LAN client a and b can PING the WAN host IP. See result 1. 
3. Then go to Network->Address objects, create a new address object, for example named My_Allow_MAC, and add LAN client b MAC address to it. 
4. Now enable GS and select My_Allow_MAC for Bypass Guest Authentication. 
5. From both LAN clients, verify if the PING access to WAN host IP is available. See result 2. 
6. Now disable 'Bypass Guest Authentication'. See Result 3.
7. From both LAN clients, verify if the PING access to WAN host IP is available. See result 4.

On general page, select HTTP as client redirect protocol; select protocol: HTTP, host 10.103.3.3, port 80 as external web server settings; 
On Auth pages, select lhm/default.aspx as login page, lhm/login.asp?rc=2 as session expiration page, lhm/login.asp?rc=3 as Idle timeout page, lhm/login.asp?rc=4 as max session page. 
On Advanced page, enable auto-session logout, set lhm/autoLogout.asp as logout CGI, enable server status check, set lhm/statusCheck.asp as server status CGI, enable session synchronization, set lhm/sessionSync.asp as session sync CGI. 
Click OK. 
3. From a DMZ client, open web browser and try to access internet. See Result 1. 
4. Disable 'External guest authentication'. See Result 2. 
5. Repeat step 3, see Result 3.
